meta.title: Rementum — Self-hosted, versioned memory for AI agents
meta.description: Rementum is a self-hosted, open-source memory layer for AI agents: versioned Markdown knowledge, staged conflict-checked writes, and OAuth-secured MCP access you control.

publicNav.banner: Free and self-hosted · star Rementum on GitHub

hero.kicker: Open source memory for AI agents
headline: Your
agents
should
remember.
hero.subtitle: Shared, versioned knowledge for every MCP client. Keep the decisions, context, and corrections that matter beyond a single conversation.
hero.clients: Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, and other MCP clients.
hero.caption: The decision stays readable. The reason it changed stays with it.
hero.exampleBodyA: An agent proposes a change against the version it read. The proposal stays separate from the current article until it is promoted.
hero.exampleBodyB: If the article has changed in the meantime, promotion stops. The conflicting write remains available for review, and the current version stays intact.

howItWorks.subtitleA: How your agents stay synchronized without overwriting each other
howItWorks.animationLabel: Illustrated overview: agents read a compact index, stage writes, and share one versioned brain

steps.title: Read
steps.description: Find an article by its title, summary, keywords, and freshness. Read the context you need without loading the whole brain.

steps.title: Stage
steps.description: Submit a write against the version you read. The proposed body stays separate from the current article.

steps.title: Check
steps.description: Rementum checks for conflicts. If the base version has changed, promotion stops so the differences can be reviewed.

steps.title: Promote
steps.description: A conflict-free promotion becomes the next encrypted, versioned article. Other agents read it on their next call.

howItWorks.title: A shared memory, with a record of change.
howItWorks.subtitle: Every article has a current version. Every proposed change has a starting point. Here is how knowledge moves between them.

say.ownNotes: Every AI agent keeps its own notes.
say.sessionEnds: The session ends. The notes are gone.
say.nothingShared: Nothing is shared between them. Nothing is versioned.
say.oneBrain: Rementum gives them one shared brain.
say.markdown: Knowledge lives in linked Markdown articles.
say.markdownSub: Self-hosted · Encrypted at rest · Every change versioned
say.everyAgent: Every agent, every session, the same current knowledge.
say.neverLoads: An agent never loads the whole brain.
say.compactIndex: It reads a compact index and opens only the article it needs.
say.everyWrite: Every write is staged, then checked against the current version.
say.promoted: Promoted as v4. Every earlier version stays in history.
say.stale: A stale write never overwrites. It waits for review instead.

pricing.subtitle: Rementum is open source, with no paid tier and no per-seat billing. You run it on your own hardware and own every byte.
pricing.priceBody: Clone it, run one install script, and connect an agent over MCP.
advantages: Free forever, with no seats, usage caps, or paywalled features
Your data stays on your server; the master key never leaves it
Unlimited brains, workspaces, agents, and versions
Full source under AGPL-3.0 to audit, fork, and extend
Runs on local models alone; no external AI provider to configure
considerations: You provide the Linux host, a domain, and open ports 80 and 443
You run updates, encrypted backups, and the occasional migration
Scaling and uptime are yours to size and monitor
No hosted SaaS tier; self-hosting is the only path today
pricing.intro: Run Rementum on your own server. The full source is yours to inspect, modify, and self-host, with no paid tier or per-seat billing.
pricing.includedA: Unlimited brains, workspaces, agents, and versions. No usage caps or paywalled features.
pricing.includedB: Local models only; no external AI provider.
pricing.handsNote: A Linux host, a domain, and ports 80 and 443. You manage updates, encrypted backups, migrations, and capacity.
